gen-eater-gf-schibsted-grotesk: Eater's thin strokes never go hairline, sitting against sturdy stems with wide gaps between letters, which gives it a dark, snarling edge. Schibsted Grotesk settles things down with open, tall-bowled shapes and terminals that never close in, friendly where the heading bites.
gen-flavors-gf-sarpanch: Flavors has a towering lowercase, with diagonals as hefty as its stems, like strokes from a stubby carpenter's pencil. Sarpanch stays compact and approachable beneath it, its lowercase e clearly open, a plain sans that lets the heading do the shouting.
gen-almendra-display-gf-noto-sans-modi: Almendra Display has an ornate, literary feel, its letters never pinching shut and its x-height standing tall. And Noto Sans Modi keeps daylight inside every curve, so if the heading were made small, that ornate charm would lose ground to the sans-serif beneath.
gen-audiowide-gf-sen: Audiowide sets its glyphs like tiles with wide grout lines. Sen sits next to it as a plain sans with a tall lowercase and curved strokes that stop before turning inward, so the futuristic heading feels softened and modern rather than cold.
gen-eater-gf-sintony: Dark, jagged and a bit menacing, Eater has thin strokes that never turn hairline and short ascenders. But Sintony gives a longer passage a smooth, unclogged read, with a chunky tall midzone that keeps the sans-serif text clear and contemporary.
gen-flavors-gf-sofia-sans: Sofia Sans reads like cut acrylic stencil pieces, tall and rounded. Flavors is the showman here, its diagonals as heavy as its stems and its x-height huge, while the sans-serif body simply keeps every line flat, modern and clear.
gen-almendra-display-gf-noto-sans-mro: Noto Sans Mro reads dense and tall through the middle of its words, with generous entrances into each letter. And Almendra Display adds its ornate, literary flourish above, letters that never pinch shut, so the plain sans below feels grounded.
gen-audiowide-gf-sono: Audiowide has a pen-plotter smoothness, with no thick-thin shift anywhere. Sono follows in a sans-serif with wide default spacing and a tall lowercase, each a left ajar, so the techy heading gets a professional, approachable partner underneath.
gen-eater-gf-sofia-sans-semi-condensed: Sofia Sans Semi Condensed has a lowercase nearly as tall as its capitals. Eater above it shimmers with mild shifts of weight and wide gaps, while the sans below keeps its stencil-cut channel constant, so a longer passage would read cleanly, with each curve visibly open.
gen-flavors-gf-stack-sans-headline: Flavors is whimsical and commanding, with a towering x-height and diagonals as hefty as its stems. But Stack Sans Headline does the quieter work, a plain sans with a monoline skeleton and wide gaps that keep tiny sizes crisp.
